subject: EU-West peering disruption — temporary traffic repointing & verification
messages:
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: ops@acme.com, infra@saasco.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: EU-West peering disruption — temporary traffic repointing & verification

Hi team,

We’re reaching out to notify you that on 2026-10-04 at ~08:40 UTC we observed a regional peering degradation affecting EU-West (eu-west-1) that is impacting request routing for a subset of tenants. Customers in affected subnets may see elevated latencies (2–4x) and a small increase in 5xxs while the infra teams work the primary path.

What we’re doing now:
- Automatically repointing traffic for affected tenants to the EU-Backup pool (eu-backup-1) to preserve availability. This will increase per-token latency for some requests but avoid timeouts.
- Enacting short-term rate smoothing to reduce amplification on the backup pool.
- Capturing KV/cache warmup metrics and detailed traces for the affected time window.

Action we need from you (Acme / SaaSCo):
1) Please confirm whether you want the traffic repointing to include cross-region fallback to US-East for your non-PII inference paths (that has higher latency but may improve throughput). Reply with YES to opt-in by 10:30 UTC today.
2) Validate that your tenant routing rules accept the temporary pool: we’ve attached a short checklist and the traffic-mapping CSV that lists current routing keys.

Attachments (stubs):
- 20261004-repointing-checklist.pdf (contains exact cname/host updates and expected DNS TTL behavior)
- eu-traffic-mapping-20261004.csv (tenant -> current/backup endpoint map)

We’ll provide a follow-up with the verification window and the post-incident summary once we stabilize. If you have a preferred validation window we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough (I’m proposing 11:00–11:30 UTC).

Apologies for the disruption — we’re prioritizing steady availability and will minimize configuration changes.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, ops@acme.com, infra@saasco.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-West peering disruption — temporary traffic repointing & verification

Irene — quick operational note and timeline details below.

Status (operational):
- 08:40 UTC: Alerts tripped for increased RTT and peer loss on primary eu-west-exchange.
- 08:52 UTC: Automated reroute kicked for 18% of affected tenants (safeguard threshold).
- 09:20 UTC: Manual repointing rolled to additional target set (total 72% of affected tenants).

Immediate steps for customers who DO NOT opt-in to cross-region fallback:
- Their traffic remains within EU on eu-backup-1. Expect median latency +40–80ms for interactive prompts, token throughput preserved.
- If you see sustained token generation throttling, notify us and we’ll enable temporary burst capacity (30m increments).

Items in attached checklist (highlight):
- DNS TTL change expectations (do NOT reduce TTL below 30s during tests).
- Validation endpoints: /health/repurpose and /metrics/repoint-status (returns JSON status).
- Suggested verification queries: small prompt with deterministic length to confirm baseline latency.

I will host the 11:00 UTC validation window and capture logs. If Acme wants US-East fallback, we need explicit opt-in by 10:30 UTC to update routing tables and notify PKI owners.

Attachments (stubs):
- 20261004-repointing-checklist.pdf
- eu-traffic-mapping-20261004.csv

Connor O
Platform Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

11:00 UTC works for the validation window — please send the meeting link. Also we saw two 5xx spikes just after 09:00 UTC; we’ll share sample request ids via the portal.

On 2026-10-04 09:45, connor_obrien@redwood.com wrote:
> Irene — quick operational note and timeline details below.

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: ops@acme.com, infra@saasco.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-06T17:04:00Z
Subject: EU-West peering disruption — post-incident summary & next steps

Hi Priya and team,

Thanks again for the rapid responses and for joining the verification window on 2026-10-04. Summary and next steps below.

What happened (short):
- Root cause: A third-party exchange experienced a control-plane regression during a config rollout which caused intermittent BGP flap for a set of EU exchange paths between 08:36–09:06 UTC.
- Impact: Approximately 9% of tenant traffic was briefly directed to suboptimal paths; we saw median RTT increase and a transient spike in 5xxs for a small subset of requests. No data was exposed and no persistent state was lost.

Mitigation timeline:
- 08:40 UTC: Alerts triggered.
- 08:52 UTC: Automatic repoint to eu-backup-1 for a safe subset.
- 09:20 UTC: Manual expansion of repointing rules to cover remaining affected tenants.
- 11:00 UTC: Verification window completed; warm caches validated.

Customer-specific notes for Acme:
- Production: Remained in EU-backup-1 as requested; observed +55ms median token latency for long prompts during the affected window.
- Staging (acme-stg-003): We exercised US-East fallback as a controlled canary — no additional action required.

Follow-up items for Redwood (owner):
- Engineer follow-up: Ben Carter will coordinate with our peering vendor to get the exact control-plane change that caused the flap (ETA 2026-10-08). Owner: ben_carter@redwood.com.
- Metrics: Naomi will publish detailed latency and 5xx timelines to the postmortem link below (ETA 2026-10-07). Owner: naomi_feldman@redwood.com.
- Customer aide: We will provide a short runbook for tenant-level verification and an optional DocuSign acknowledgement for SLA credit requests if needed.

Public artifacts and links:
- Postmortem (internal): https://redwood-internal.company/postmortems/EU-WEST-2026-10-04
- Repointing checklist (artifact): attached (20261004-repointing-checklist.pdf)

If you’d like a formal RCA call, we can schedule that next week — please let me know preferred windows.

Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for coordinating rapidly.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference
